# Bitfroest.fs 0.0.54

Changes since version [0.0.53](https://github.com/s-a/Bitfroest.fs/releases/tag/v0.0.53).

## Added

- In the Bitfroest file context menu, **Send to** lists configured favorites. Choose a favorite and select **Copy** or **Move** to review the selection and destination in the standard transfer dialog. The optional Windows system context menu has its own entries.

## Improved

- The file manager button is now on the left side of the VS Code Status Bar.
- During copy and move, the status bar shows the source file currently being transferred. The overall byte count covers the selection across conflict prompts when file sizes are known. Skipped files are excluded from the remaining total.
- **Copy Details** includes available transfer context, error codes, and the last confirmed step. It shortens recognized private paths and keeps stack frame locations. The activity log records transfer decisions, cancellations, and outcomes.

## Fixed

- Copy and move use the confirmed source and destination paths. Unrelated open and cached folders stay outside transfer validation. A preparation error identifies the blocking folder and the failed check when available.
- Moving a folder into an existing folder of the same name keeps destination-only files, including files added or replaced during the transfer. File conflicts use the standard transfer policy. On Windows, the merge also handles folder names that differ only in capitalization.
- Folder preparation can verify directory entries directly when the filesystem returns missing timestamps.
- Copy, move, and delete update affected entries in open folder tabs without relisting the folders. Copy and move keep the current column widths. Deleting from a folder that is still loading keeps the other visible entries in place.
- The status bar reports when a confirmed transfer leaves all selected files or folders unchanged. Windows transfer progress failures include the underlying error.

## Updating

Update Bitfroest.fs in the VS Code Extensions view on the pre-release channel. The supported packages target Windows x64 and Linux x64. The Apple Silicon package is experimental. macOS has no official support.
